what: Every piece of state in RareFriends, written down once, with exactly one home. This file is the
schema M3 item 6 asks for: something the code reads, not prose. It names FIELDS, TYPES, HOMES and
SOURCES. It carries NO VALUES - not one number - because values are the economist's and the
deployer's, and because a number written here would be a second home for it. schemacheck.js
enforces that: there is no JSON number anywhere under `entities`, `enums` or `oneHome`.
It is JSON and not a document, not a .d.ts, not a .proto and not annotated Solidity, for four
reasons that are all about this repository rather than about taste:
1. estate/ has NO package.json and NO node_modules. Every check in it is plain Node with zero
dependencies. A JSON-Schema validator, protobuf or a TypeScript type would be the first
dependency estate/ ever had, and it would be a dependency of the schema itself.
2. There is no hardhat and no foundry; solc 0.8.36 is called directly. So the schema cannot be
an annotation on Solidity - the Solidity does not exist yet (M20 writes it). The schema has
to be the thing the Solidity is checked AGAINST, which means a declaration a plain-Node check
can compare a .sol file's structs to. gencheck.js already does exactly this for the HP table.
3. Both halves of the codebase can read JSON with nothing added: Node `require`, and a page
`fetch`. base-data.json is the precedent for the page half.
4. It is INERT. index.html's ECON became a client belief by being assembled out of 25 live
constants; a schema that can compute is a schema that will. Nothing here evaluates.

homes.chain: A slot, a mapping entry or an event on chain 4663. The only home a thing can be argued about from.
homes.map: Frozen into a map at its seed. Reproducible from the seed and the generator version; never stored.
homes.client: A client belief. Redrawable, guessable, and worth nothing in a dispute. DESIGN's third home.
homes.server: OUR SERVER'S LIVE RECORD - Redis where it helps - which decides every fight and is the authority for v1 (DESIGN, Fights resolve on our server, and we are the authority for v1; the deployer, 2026-09-30). THE FOURTH HOME, added for M3 item 5: the first three were written before that ruling and the schema had nowhere to put what our server holds. What lives here is the game AS IT IS PLAYED - a base, its tiles, buildings, crews, posts and fights. The chain holds that game's RECORD, not its state: a session's changes in one write (decision 9), a hash of every fight as it happens (fightHash, RareFightLog.commitFight, RECORD_FIGHT), and an hourly sync head (syncHead, RareFightLog.commitSync, RECORD_SYNC; rulings 16 and 18). On a mismatch the server's record stands and the deployer is alerted (ruling 3). A player signs nothing and pays nothing for a fight. V2 moves on chain (ruling 5). Server-homed state is ours to change at any time, which is why a power's Working power, Speed, Reach and Sight need nothing on chain.

typesNote: mapping(address => bool) is a per-address lookup: a page reads it one address at a time (whitelisted(addr)) and can never enumerate it - there is no list on chain to show. deployer.html's whitelist add/remove rows already treat it that way. Ruling 21. The two bytes32 mappings are ShadowFriends' per-mint state (shadowed, revokedAt), keyed by the raw Solana mint and read the same way: one key at a time, never enumerated.

gaps.note: BINDING.md §12's eight rows, keyed so an entity can name the one it closes. `covered` says whether THIS file gives it a home; it never claims a contract exists - M20 builds them.

baseState.was: No contract holds a tile, a building, a level, a finished-or-building flag, a watchtower's occupant, a wall's crew, or a Friend's post. base.defense() is the specification and it exists only in the page

rulesOnChain.was: The rules table lives in base.ECON in index.html - a client belief. Five of its fields are PROPOSED

rulesIdInRecord.was: DESIGN's replay list is 'the word, line-ups and spots'. The numbers are not in it, so a recorded fight does not name the table it was fought under

ordersCommitment.was: Decided in approach, M20's to design, nothing built. No commitment, no reveal, no consequence for not revealing

rosterStorage.was: The line-up row { collection, tokenId, gen, x, y, tower, order, fx, fy } has no home. §4.4 says every field of it is chain state; none of it is

fightLifecycle.was: No state machine, no fight id, no LinedUp/Rolling/Settled, no FightSealed

disputeProcess.was: No submitter, no bond, no challenge window, no deadline. 'Dispute' appears once in DESIGN. BINDING §18 says this is the largest hole in the whole file
disputeProcess.why: DECLINED FOR V1 BY THE DEPLOYER, 2026-09-30 (Fights resolve on our server: 'None. No dispute machinery and no $RF bond escrow in v1. Both deferred, on purpose'), and the reason is No diamond's first tier: a contract custodying a bond is permanent, and a permanent contract for a deferred mechanism cannot be corrected and is not wanted yet. What stands in its place is AUDITABILITY, not trust: fightHash as the fight happens and syncHead every hour, so history cannot be quietly rewritten even though we decide it. fight.bond and fight.challengeDeadline stay reserved so V2 has a named place. The hole is not filled; it is declined, by a ruling and not by this file.

rentedFriendOwner.was: base.defense() marks defenders rented:true and the mockup fields three of them. Part one §2.1 checks ownerOf(tokenId) == msg.sender at join. Nothing in DESIGN says whether a rented Friend defends, or who counts as its owner for that check
rentedFriendOwner.why: `rosterRow.postedBy` and the `hire` entity give the question somewhere to land, but WHICH address the join guard checks is the deployer's (BINDING §13 item 7).

enums.note: `members` is ordered; a member's on-chain value is its index, from zero. An enum with `decided: false` has an empty members list on purpose: nobody has said what belongs in it, and an empty list is countable where a guess is not.

home.note: DESIGN's classification - three homes, and a fourth since the ruling that fights resolve on our server (M3 item 5). Not on chain; this file's own vocabulary.

behaviour.note: THE SIX BEHAVIOURS A POWER MAY TOUCH - a decided, closed list (decision 8), in the order DESIGN's 'Adding a power is data, not code' gives them: Strength, Working power, Speed, Reach / travel means, Sight, Ownership. power.amounts is indexed by this. A new ability needs new code only if it does something none of the six can say, and that is a new rule inside the fight - which is why the fight is replaceable and this list is closed. schemacheck holds the members and their order to DESIGN.md's table.

order.note: A defender's standing order. combat.js ORDERS and RareCombat.Defender.order read the index, so the ORDER OF THIS LIST IS CONSENSUS - moving a member changes every recorded fight.

side.note: The side an attack comes in from. combat.js SIDES. The vector is derived from the base's tile bounding box, never supplied - BINDING §10.3.

fightState.note: BINDING §11.5, §11.6 and §16.2. `settled` is one-shot and terminal: the same fight cannot credit the scoreboard twice. `none` is index zero so an unwritten slot is not a live state, which is the RareDuel.State pattern.

duelState.note: Already deployed shape, copied here rather than restated. Members keep their Solidity spelling because schemacheck compares them to the .sol file character for character.

stakeCurrency.note: COORDINATION POINT, NOT A DECISION MADE HERE. BINDING §20.1 as written says 'you bet with crystals not RF', crystals only. The deployer has since allowed a duel to be staked in EITHER, and a second chain-engineer is specifying it in BINDING. Two members are recorded so the schema has a place for a discriminator; which members survive is theirs and the deployer's, and §20.1 must be reconciled before M20.

buildingKind.note: THESE ARE THE SETTLED CODE NAMES (M2 item 6) PLUS THE NINTH, THE CAPACITOR (M8 item 11, decided as a building of its own), AND THEY ARE NOT A SOLIDITY ENUM. M3 item 4 requires that adding a building be an identity and a row of numbers with no code change; a Solidity enum is a code change and an upgrade. So a building's kind is a `uint16 kindId` into the stored `buildingType` registry, and this list is the nine rows that registry starts with - not its ceiling. index.html's KIND object is the client's copy of those rows, and `oneHome` says so.

job.note: M3 item 2 requires 'a Friend's job'. DESIGN names chopping, harvesting, standing watch, manning a wall and science at a cell, but never as a closed list, and a Friend posted at a cell for science is doing a job AND holding a post. Needs the game engineer plus the deployer; M8/M9/M11 territory.

gameState.note: BUILT as RareGame.State by the chain engineer from the decided clocks (join window, start delay, length) and the decided end (the winners are declared); `Abandoned` is joining closing short of the minimum with every stake refunded. The members are the contract's, not the deployer's: PROPOSED, and the steward owes the deployer the question. `None` is index zero so an unwritten slot is not a live state - the RareDuel.State pattern.

moveKind.note: `rebuild` (M13 item 14, rulings 69 and 77) puts back a LOST keep - one an opponent destroyed or its owner knocked down (`keepLost`): a client move, for the keep row's `rebuild` bill (75 wood and 75 crystals), at level 1 on a free tile, taking that bill's raise time (`rebuildMs`); the first keep is placed with `build` and is free, and `build` refuses a keep on a base that lost one. Until the rebuilt keep is finished nothing on that base is raised or placed. `attacked` also carries `destroyed`, the other buildings an attack destroyed: a destroyed silo or collection depot SPILLS what the base then holds above its store onto a free tile next to it (rulings 70 and 107 (1)), and nothing destroyed is refunded (ruling 106) - no fight writes it yet, because combat.js fights wall sections only. `harvesterLost` is a harvester destroyed in an attack, written by OUR SERVER on the defender's record (record.js settleHarvester; the deployer approved it 2026-10-01): its depot runs one fewer, no refund (rulings 15 and 56), and what it carried spills on its tile (rulings 70 and 88). `hands` (M8 item 3) is how many Friends work a building going up, from a moment on - the action a player takes when they put Friends on a build or pull them off it. `attack` and `attacked` (M13 item 2) are one fight's result, written by OUR SERVER and never by a client (rulings 3 and 7; record.js SERVER_MOVES, refused in a client's batch by serve.py): `attack` on the attacker's record - its Friends that went down leave the roster; `attacked` on the defender's - its Friends that went down and its broken wall sections come off, and a won attack destroys the keep (ruling 37 (d)), after which nothing on that base can be raised. NEITHER MOVES A PURSE (ruling 68, superseding ruling 14): resources are won only by claiming the building, and a fight move naming any non-zero loot is refused. The move log's discriminator. §17.2.2 makes every move an event folded into moveRoot, so THIS LIST IS THE DEFINITION OF WHAT COUNTS AS HISTORY - a move kind left off it is a thing that happened and is not in the record. DECIDED (the deployer, 2026-09-30): 'all actions should be saved' - EVERY ACTION A PLAYER TAKES IS A MOVE. The members are estate/record.js's MOVES table, the actions the page gives a player today, and recordcheck holds the two lists equal; a later milestone that gives the player a new action (a fight, a duel, the market's verbs, a claim of ground) adds its kind to both, never an action the record does not carry. M18 closes the game against it. Not a move, by the same ruling: when the player was last on the map (base lastSeen in record.js), which a session with no moves still writes; what happens while a player is idle is recorded through other players' actions. `stakeHeld` and `stakeSettled` (M17 items 4 and 5) are a challenge's stake on the real base purse, written by OUR SERVER (estate/duels.py) and never by a client (record.js SERVER_MOVES): `stakeHeld` takes the stake out of the purse at accept and holds it against the duel; `stakeSettled` releases that hold and credits the side's unspent hold and winnings, spilling what the store cannot hold onto the tile next to the keep (rulings 70 and 80) - a duel settled twice is refused by the record itself. `hands` (M8 item 3) is how many Friends work a building going up, from a moment on - the action a player takes when they put Friends on a build or pull them off it. `attack` and `attacked` (M13 item 2) are one fight's result, written by OUR SERVER and never by a client (rulings 3 and 7; record.js SERVER_MOVES, refused in a client's batch by serve.py): `attack` on the attacker's record - its Friends that went down leave the roster and a won attack brings the loot home; `attacked` on the defender's - its Friends that went down and its broken wall sections come off, and a won attack takes the whole purse (ruling 14) and destroys the keep (ruling 37 (d)), after which nothing on that base can be raised. The move log's discriminator. §17.2.2 makes every move an event folded into moveRoot, so THIS LIST IS THE DEFINITION OF WHAT COUNTS AS HISTORY - a move kind left off it is a thing that happened and is not in the record. DECIDED (the deployer, 2026-09-30): 'all actions should be saved' - EVERY ACTION A PLAYER TAKES IS A MOVE. The members are estate/record.js's MOVES table, the actions the page gives a player today, and recordcheck holds the two lists equal; a later milestone that gives the player a new action (a fight, a duel, the market's verbs, a claim of ground) adds its kind to both, never an action the record does not carry. M18 closes the game against it. Not a move, by the same ruling: when the player was last on the map (base lastSeen in record.js), which a session with no moves still writes; what happens while a player is idle is recorded through other players' actions.

closeReason.note: Why a game ended. BINDING §16.4 last bullet: an era must not close with fights still open, and what happens if it does is undecided.

player.note: Who a player is. NOT a row we invent: a player IS an address, and what they hold is held by tokens and by per-game accumulators. This entity exists so the schema has one place to say that - and to say that a player has no profile row at all, save the one name they may choose (M5 item 2), which our server keeps beside the records and shows with the address.

addr.note: The identity. There is no id and no registration: an address that holds a Genesis can join a game. A chosen `name` sits beside it and never replaces it.

genesisHeld.note: Derived, not stored: ownerOf over the Genesis collection. Storing it is a second home for ownership and it would go stale on every transfer.

name.note: M5 item 2. DESIGN, Who a player is: 'a player can choose a name, and their address is always visible with it. A name is theirs to pick and change.' OVERRIDDEN HOME: held by our server (estate/names.py, beside the records, keyed by address), set only by the wallet's own signed-in session, and never chain state. Every screen that shows it shows `addr` beside it, so a name is never a disguise. Unique per server, compared folded (case, separators and look-alikes); never shaped like an address.

genesis.note: The Genesis token. M3 item 8, DECIDED: the Genesis token owns the base, and the base's purse is that token's own account. So selling a base is a token transfer and not a bespoke function, which is why it had to be settled before M20.

collection.note: The Genesis contract. Named rather than assumed because the roster row carries a collection too and the two must be comparable.

tokenId.note: Together with `collection`, the owner of a base.

account.note: tokenBoundAccount(tokenId). DERIVED - the toolkit computes it, so storing it is a second home. This is the base's purse; the deployer's words were 'it should be the Genesis NFT wallet, they all come with one'.

friend.note: A Friend, as a token. Its generation is READ FROM THE CHAIN AND NEVER SUPPLIED - gencheck.js enforces that no deployable contract commits state or moves a token on a generation it was handed. Everything a Friend is, except where it is standing in a game, belongs to the token and not to us.

collection.note: The Friends contract. Not assumed to be one address: the roster row is keyed by collection AND tokenId because partnerships bring other collections in.

tokenId.note: The unit. DESIGN §1: a unit is a token, never a generation.

gen.note: 1 to 6. READ, never supplied: generation(tokenId) on the collection. The single most-guarded value in the game - BINDING §10 ranks a forged generation fourth of seven and gencheck.js exists for it alone.

family.note: M3 item 2's 'family'. Read from the collection's own metadata, not stored by us. Named so nothing later stores a copy.

seed.note: The token's own seed, which the sprite is drawn from. Read from the collection.

wallet.note: tokenBoundAccount(tokenId) - every Friend has one, the marketplace is built on it, and nothing has used it yet.

hire.note: A rented Friend: hired from a holder who owns no Genesis, so it can man a wall or a tower for somebody else's base. index.html fields three of them on random free tiles today. THIS ENTITY IS A PLACE FOR AN UNANSWERED QUESTION, not an answer: BINDING §12's last row and §13 item 7 ask whether a rented Friend defends at all and whose ownership check it passes, and that is the deployer's.

holder.note: Who owns the token and is letting it out. The join guard's ownerOf check passes against THIS unless the deployer says otherwise.

game.note: A hire is per game, because a game's numbers are frozen and a hire is a number.

fee.note: NO VALUE AND NO UNIT DECIDED. Whether a hire is paid in crystals or $RF, once or per game, is the economist's and the deployer's.

map.note: THE ONE ENTITY WHOSE HOME IS THE SEED. Everything here is reproducible from the seed plus the generator's version, so none of it is stored - and the generator's version is stored WITH the seed, because a seed without the code that read it reproduces nothing. That pairing is the whole reason this home exists.

seed.note: OVERRIDDEN HOME: the seed itself is chain state on the game row. It is the anchor; everything below is what it unfolds into.

generatorVersion.note: OVERRIDDEN HOME, and §19.1 names it explicitly. Chain state beside the seed. A generator change with the version unchanged silently re-draws every recorded game.

hill.note: The height field. index.html's HILL - derived from the seed by mapgen.js, never stored.

waterSites.note: Tile x,y pairs where water runs. index.html's WATER_SITES. A generator may only stand on one, which is why placement reads this.

seams.note: Crystal seams, tile x,y pairs. index.html's SEAM_PLAN.

groves.note: Tree groves, tile x,y pairs. index.html's GROVES.

baseSites.note: Where a base may be planted. mapcheck already proves 100 of these are reproducible from the seed.

game.note: A game, and the row that makes every other row replayable. `rulesId` freezes the numbers; `moveRoot` and `moveCount` chain the history together - one word and a counter, and BINDING §19.1 calls them THE NEW THING the deployer's 'we keep the scoreboard and the moves' answer adds to the schema.

id.note: The game. Every other row in the schema that is per game points at this, and a number frozen per game is frozen against it.

mapSeed.note: The map. Stored, because the map's home is the seed and the seed's home is here.

generatorVersion.note: The code that reads the seed. Stored beside it or the pair is worthless.

rulesId.note: The keccak of the rules table this game was created with, written once and never again. NO NUMBER CHANGES DURING A RUNNING GAME - every number, not just money - and this id is what makes that claim checkable rather than a promise. BINDING §16.3: because the table a fight was fought under cannot have moved, a recorded fight can always be replayed.

cutBps.note: The house's cut, in bps. A stored value and not a constant, because anything the deployer page can change is stored state - 'No diamond'. No value here.

cutFrozen.note: Set true at the first payment. §19.1's 'frozen-at-first-payment flag'.

places.note: How many ranked places pay, deployer-set per game, at most MAX_PLACES (10). RareGame.Game.places. The SPLIT is a rule and not a field (DESIGN, Starting a game): 50 / 30 / the rest equally - RareGame.split(prize, n) is that rule as a pure function, so no share is stored.

minPlayers.note: The fewest players a game needs to start. PROPOSED 2 (the economist's), not decided; a parameter with a starting value, never a constant. RareGame.Game.minPlayers.

demo.note: The demo bit the game was created under, frozen for its life. BINDING §28; RareRoles.requireMayJoin reads it. RareGame.Game.demo.

length.note: How long the game runs, seconds. Starting value seven days, the deployer's or the gamemaster's to set. RareGame.Game.length; closesAt = startsAt + length.

cut.note: In $RF: what left the pot for feeTo AT START (DESIGN: the cut is taken at game start). RareGame.Game.cut.

starter.note: Who opened the game and set its entry; the first player. RareGame.Game.starter.

players.note: The roster, in join order. RareGame.Game.players; inGame(id, who) is the per-address lookup.

joinClosesAt.note: When joining shuts. The start screen's first clock.

startsAt.note: When play begins. The second clock.

closesAt.note: When the game ends and the pot pays.

pot.note: In $RF. The pot pays the three ranked places; a duel is staked separately - see stakeCurrency.

moveRoot.note: The running hash: moveRoot = keccak256(abi.encode(moveRoot, move)), one word, updated in the same transaction as the move. BUILT in RareGame (M6 item 5, 2026-10-01), keyed by game id, folded from zero as keccak256(abi.encode(moveRoot, uint64 game, actor, kind, seq, body)) - every input is in the move event. NOT record.js's head (BINDING §64.7). BINDING §17.3 is the six free reads a player uses to prove the history is intact. §17.4 is the honest limit: it proves the record is INTACT, never that it is TRUE.

moveCount.note: How many moves are folded in. Lets a reader know when they have fetched them all.

finalScoreboard.note: The scoreboard frozen at close. §19.1's last row: a later game or the marketplace may read it, and a live accumulator is not a result.

rules.note: THE RULES TABLE, and the largest gap BINDING found: it was base.ECON in index.html, assembled by Combat.rulesFrom() - a client belief - until M3 item 1 moved every number in it to estate/values.js, the one home it has until M20 writes it to chain; Combat.rulesFrom() now reads it from there and base.ECON is a view of it. BINDING §10 ranks forging it FIRST of seven, ahead of deleting the walls, because it is not one number about one body, it is all the numbers about all the bodies. Written once per game, frozen for it, addressed by rulesId, never a Solidity constant.

hp.note: By fight SLOT, 11 entries: 1 to 6 the Friends' generations (values.js HP_OF, it was index.html's; gencheck.js holds it to one source); 0 a 1/1 Doopie, 1140 (HP_OF[0], ruling 55); 7 to 10 an ordinary Doopie of Evolution 1 to 4 (values.js DOOPIE_HP, 225 / 337 / 506 / 759 - its own table, not linked to HP_OF: rulings 81 and 86). Every weapon column of a Doopie slot is the Friend generation's that values.js DOOPIE_ARMS names (ruling 85): Evolution 1 the spear, 2 the bow, 3 the crossbow, 4 and the 1/1 the catapult.

reach.note: By generation, IN SPOTS - a spot is half a tile, so a weapon's tile range doubles here. Integers only; the Solidity is a line-for-line copy.

period.note: By generation, ms between shots. COMBAT.periodMs by weapon class.

area.note: By generation, splash radius in spots.

vsBuilding.note: By generation, the multiplier against a building.

wallHp.note: A level-1 wall section. BINDING §16.3's own example of why the freeze matters: a fight fought at one wallHp and replayed at another produces two truths about two worlds.

towerReach.note: How much further a Friend up a watchtower can shoot, in spots. COMBAT.towerRange doubled.

dropReach.note: How far a wall crew can drop stones, in spots. COMBAT.dropRange doubled.

coverDiv.note: DECIDED, ruling 45: a Friend standing ON a wall (its crew) is hit 1/coverDiv as often - 50% protection, so coverDiv is two - and a Friend BEHIND a wall gets no cover at all. The rule moved, not just the number: both engines used to halve the chance for a Friend behind a wall (M13 item 9). One reading is stated rather than chosen in the ruling: '50% protection' is read as halving the chance a shot lands, not halving the damage.

stepMs.note: THE WALKING SPEED, as the struct holds it. DECIDED, ruling 44: every Friend walks at `speed`, ONE TILE A SECOND, and it is a DEPLOYER SETTING (the deployer tunes it after testing; deployer.html carries the row). The struct carries no `speed` field: it stores the step that speed implies, stepMs = 1000 / (2 x speed) because a spot is half a tile - five hundred ms a spot at the decided speed (combat.js rulesFrom, P.speed). So `speed` is the deployer's number and this field is its encoding; the two are one setting, not two, and a page must edit speed and write stepMs, never let the two be set apart.

defendReach.note: How far a DEFEND order may stray from its post, IN SPOTS. DECIDED, ruling 46: FIVE TILES, which is ten spots (combat.js rulesFrom, spots(P.defendTiles)). A deployer setting, written per game and frozen with the rest of the table like every number here.

splashFalloff.note: PROPOSED, no value, AND NOT IN RareCombat.Rules TODAY. DESIGN says 'the splash falling off by half a spot'; §10.1.3 counts it among the five, and the struct has no field for it. So the table is one field short of the specification and schemacheck records the mismatch rather than hiding it.

entryGap.note: NO VALUE, AND IT MAY NOT BELONG HERE AT ALL. BINDING §10.3.3: the mockup offers three gaps and defaults to one, DESIGN says only 'in a line off the base', and WHETHER THE ATTACKER PICKS IT is the deployer's. If the attacker picks it, it is a fight field and not a rules field. Declared here with that fork written down.

buildingType.note: THE BUILDING REGISTRY, and M3 items 3 and 4 in one row. A building's placement rule and its footprint are DATA THE ROW CARRIES, not code, so a new building is an identity and a row of numbers. It WAS index.html's KIND object plus WOOD_COST plus SILO_CAP plus CELL_REACH plus CELL_NEEDS plus lockReason() - five constants and a function, in five places. Since M3 item 1 it is one row a kind in estate/values.js `kinds` - levelName, crystalCost, woodCost, capacity, reach, footprint, placement - and the page's five names read columns of it.

kindId.note: The identity. A NUMBER AND NOT AN ENUM MEMBER, which is the whole of M3 item 4's first case: a new building is a new row with a new id, and no contract is redeployed. The nine starting rows are `buildingKind`'s members - the ninth, the capacitor, landed in values.js on 2026-09-30 (M8 item 11) and is the first row the game reads that the contracts have never named: its kindId is the chain engineer's to number.

codeName.note: The settled name: keep, hut, silo, tower, wall, cell, generator, collectionDepot (M2 item 6).

levels.note: How many levels the row defines. M3 item 4's second case: adding a level is a row of numbers, so every per-level field below is an array this long and nothing is a fixed-size struct.

crystalCost.note: Per level. KIND[k].cost. No values. HOME: RareRules.setLadder/ladderOf, per rulesId, frozen by RareRules.freeze - M15 item 11's chain half.

woodCost.note: Per level. KIND[k].wood - the logs each level takes, paid beside crystalCost at every level that names both (ruling 76: level 1 wood only, level 2 half and half, level 3 crystals), and that mix is data rather than a rule in code. HOME: RareRules, beside crystalCost. Not refunded by a demolition (BINDING §46.4).

buildMs.note: Per level: how long ONE Friend takes to raise this kind to that level (M8 item 2). DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep row 24: four seconds of one Friend's work per unit (1.00) of the rung's materials, wood and crystals added together - so every kind's per-level buildMs is DERIVED from that one number (values.js buildMsPerUnit) and the rung's own price, and a free rung (Keep I) takes no time. A deployer setting. The flat demo pace (2.8 s a level) loads ONLY under the explicit demo switch (pace=demo, RF_PACE=demo; values.js demoPace) and is a demo, not a value. record.js raiseMs reads it.

hands.note: The ceiling on Friends working one build (M8 item 3): each Friend up to it takes the time down linearly - buildMs / n - and past it another adds nothing. DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep rows 25 and 27: linear, up to 4 for every one-tile building, 2 for a wall (an edge with two faces, one crew a side), 4 for the capacitor. A deployer setting. record.js `ceiling` and `worked` read it.

strength.note: Per level. M3 item 2's 'strength'. DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep rows 6 and 7: each level doubles from the kind's first (keep 1,500 / 3,000 / 6,000; a wall 400 / 800 / 1,600; Cell IV 2,000; the capacitor the generator's ladder, 200 to 1,600), and NO BUILDING MAY EXCEED THE CITADEL'S 6,000 - values.js `strengthMax`, which refuses to load a row over it, so the ceiling is a rule and not a note. A harvester is not a building row and has its own, 150 (values.js `harvStrength`, row 6). A wall's level 1 names WALL_HP, the fight's own (rules.wallHp - see oneHome, it is declared in two places and one must go). THE FIGHT IS BEHIND THIS ROW: combat.js and RareCombat.sol give every wall WALL_HP whatever its level and target no other building, so levels 2 and 3 of a wall and every other kind's strength are decided numbers no fight reads yet - owed with the parity check.

energy.note: Per level, in P: what the building DRAWS while it runs (M8 item 10). DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep rows 29 and 30: by kind and level in values.js (a cell 2 / 4 / 8 / 14, a depot 3 / 6 / 10, the keep 0 / 2 / 6; a generator and a capacitor draw nothing). index.html's energy tick (M10 item 4) reads it: a base's demand is the sum of its standing buildings' draws, its supply the sum of their `supply`, and a building whose draw cannot be met is marked stalled and its bar reads the shortfall. NOT IN RareRules YET: the contract side is a spec for the chain engineer.

supply.note: Per level, in P: what the building MAKES while it runs. Only the generator's row carries it. DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep row 31: 10 / 25 / 60 - a level-1 base runs on its water wheel, just. A row without the column makes nothing.

release.note: Per level, in P: the most a STORE lets out when the generator it serves is offline. Only the capacitor's row carries it. DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep row 32: 15 / 40 / 100 / 250. A store's `capacity` is what it holds, in P·h - the same column a silo uses for crystals, because it is the one number the kind caps.

leak.note: Per level, in percent of the store lost a day. Only the capacitor's row carries it, and it is DECIDED: 10, 5, 3, none (Energy, 'Two ladders, and they are independent'). How fast a store CHARGES is not a column: it is set by the source, and which generator level each of 48 h / 24 h / 6 h / 2 h belongs to is undecided, so nothing holds it.

capacity.note: Per level, the one number the kind caps: a depot's crystals (what it holds; DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep row 20: 240.00 / 720.00 / 2,160.00), a silo's crystals (what it ADDS to the depot's reserve - How much you can hold; record.js storeCap; DECIDED, ruling 64, row 21: +300 / +900 / +3,000), THE KEEP'S FLOOR (DECIDED, ruling 62, sweep row 45: 240.00 at every keep level while the keep stands - a floor under the store that counts only when no depot and no silo stores, not an addition; once the keep is gone and nothing else stores, the cap is `rebuild`'s crystals instead (ruling 78), so the base can gather its way back to a keep; record.js storeCap reads it through placement.isKeep, not the kind's name), a wall's crew (WALL_CAP), a capacitor's store (ruling 64, row 32). One field because they are one concept, and the note on the row says which. A depot's harvesters are one a level, not this column; a hut holds no Friends (housing is not a thing).

rebuild.note: RULING 77: what putting back a LOST keep costs, one amount per material keyed by the purse's own field names (record.js MATERIALS), the shape a level's bill has - it comes back at level 1, and the first keep stays free. Only a row whose placement isKeep carries it. RULING 78: its crystals are also the store of a base with no keep, no depot and no silo (record.js storeCap), so a player who has lost everything can gather their way back. The rebuild move itself is M13 item 14; this field's chain home is M3 item 9.

reach.note: Per level, in spots: a cell's claim (CELL_REACH), a tower's sight. Zero for a kind that reaches nowhere.

footprint.note: RELATIVE TILE OFFSETS, x,y pairs. A one-tile building is a single [0,0]. DATA, so a building bigger than one tile needs no code change - which matters because wallsortcheck's uncovered column says 'buildings bigger than one tile, which do not exist yet' and this is the field that lets them.

placement.note: The rule as data. M3 item 3.

abilityId.note: A POWER A BUILDING CARRIES - IF A BUILDING MAY CARRY ONE, which is the deployer's (Still open for the deployer: can a building carry a power, and can a power act on someone else - recommended yes, not decided). This note used to say adding an ability is NEW BEHAVIOUR THAT NO ROW CAN CARRY and that this field points at code; it was written before decision 8, which says the opposite: adding an ability is a ROW (the `power` entity), and only the fight and the dice that decide a fight ever need replacing. If the deployer says yes, this becomes a ref to power like item.abilityId; if no, the field goes and the growth table's two building examples with it. HELD BACK as (d) of What has to be replaceable until then - the type and the field are as they were, the claim is not.

addedInGame.note: The game id from which this row exists. A row added mid-game would change a running game's numbers, which the freeze forbids - so a new building becomes available to the NEXT game, and this field is what makes that enforceable instead of remembered.

placementRule.note: Where a building may stand, as data. It WAS lockReason() in index.html - two lines that knew only about the keep - plus the water test for a generator, plus CELL_NEEDS for a cell's science, spread across the placement code. Every one of them is a field here, and since M3 item 3 every kind's row in values.js carries one in exactly this shape (schemacheck holds the keys to these fields): lockReason() reads needsKeep, isKeep and maxPerBase and knows no building by name. onWater and onBaseEdge are still tested by the placement code in tap() rather than read off the row - M9's lock, not M3's.

needsKeep.note: Nothing can stand until the keep does. lockReason()'s only real rule today.

isKeep.note: One to a base, and the thing every other row waits on. lockReason()'s other branch.

cappedByKeepLevel.note: 'No building can be raised past the keep's own tier' - the keep's own sub-line, which is a rule living in a display string.

onWater.note: A generator needs running water: map.waterSites. terraincheck already proves a generator is refused on dry ground.

onBaseEdge.note: A wall stands on a tile's edge, not in its middle - which is why a wall carries a direction and nothing else does.

onClaimedGround.note: A cell may be placed on claimed ground to push further still.

maxPerBase.note: Zero for no limit. A fight has NO limit on wall sections (deployer, 2026-10-01): RareCombat's MAX_WALLS of 16 is removed and every finished section is fought, so this field is a building rule only, never a combat bound. No value - it is the deployer's.

scienceGen.note: Per level, the worst generation that can run it - CELL_NEEDS. Zero where no posted Friend is needed. Per level because a cell's second level needs a Gen 3 and its fourth a Gen 1.

needsKind.note: A kindId this one requires, or zero. Named rather than hard-coded so a partnership's building can require a partner's. index.html's lockReason() reads it since M8 item 4: a kind whose needsKind is not standing finished on the base is locked in the catalogue. No row sets it today.

nextToKind.note: THE FOURTH PLACEMENT RULE (Energy): a kindId this one must stand TOUCHING - sharing a tile edge with - or zero. The capacitor's row names the generator, and touching is also what binds the store to the generator it serves ('What a capacitor backs up: the one it touches'). index.html's siteReason() reads it in tap(); the kind is written by codeName until M20 numbers the registry.

economy.note: THE ECONOMY'S TABLE - every number M4 item 4 puts on the deployer page that is neither the fight's (rules) nor a building's (buildingType). FOUND BY THE EXTRACTION, NOT BY THE FIRST PASS: M3 item 2's list of pieces named the purse and the rules and never the numbers the purse grows by, so when they left index.html for estate/values.js there was no entity to map them to. 'Anything the deployer page can change is stored state on chain, never a constant' (M3 item 1), and every one of these is on M4's page. Frozen per game like rules - No number changes under a running game - so its home is a row beside rules, addressed by the same rulesId. M4 item 4 also names a seam's yield per growth stage, the depot's cap and what a silo adds; those are not constants in the page today and are not invented here - the economist's to add when they are.

crystalUnit.note: Crystals and wood are stored in hundredths; every display divides by this. values.js crystalUnit; index.html CRYSTAL_UNIT reads it.

startPurse.note: What a base is created holding, in hundredths. values.js startPurse; the running purse is base.crystals, the record's base row (M6, record.js baseRow), restored on open and written with the session.

yearDiv.note: A game year is the game's length divided by this - DECIDED a quarter (How long a game year is), and a divisor rather than a fraction because a chain cannot hold 0.25. Shown on the deployer page, not edited there: 'the year itself needs no field'. values.js yearDiv; index.html GAME_YEAR_OF is 1 / it.

growMs.note: A seam's full growth cycle, stages every quarter. values.js growMs.

handYield.note: Crystals a Friend cuts from a seam by hand. values.js handYield.

stageYieldBps.note: What a seam gives by growth stage, in basis points of a full haul (M10 item 2: taking it young gives less). As many stages as entries, each an equal share of growMs. DECIDED, ruling 64, sweep row 16: 25% / 50% / 75% / 100% at stages 0 to 3. A deployer setting. values.js stageYieldBps; record.js haulOf reads it for the harvester and the hand alike.

harvCost.note: What a harvester costs to build, in hundredths. values.js harvCost.

treeWood.note: Wood a tree gives when felled, in hundredths (three logs). values.js treeWood. NOT trees per grove - that is a map parameter, frozen at the seed, and mapgen.js carries it.

chopMs.note: How long one chop takes. values.js chopMs.

regrowMs.note: How long a felled tree takes to stand again. values.js regrowMs.

unlock.note: WHAT THE GAME YEAR OPENS, one row a thing. Today one row, the capacitor: a water mill (the generator's level 2) standing for one game year is its prerequisite (DESIGN, How long a game year is). index.html's UNLOCKS was the only copy; values.js `unlocks` is the home, keyed by what it opens, and the page turns afterYears into milliseconds of its own clock. A row and not a constant so that what the year opens next is a row added, not code.

opens.note: What the row opens - 'capacitor' today. Becomes a kindId the day the capacitor is a buildingType row (M8 item 11).

needsKind.note: The kindId whose standing starts the countdown. values.js writes it by codeName (needs.type) because the registry is keyed by name until M20 numbers it.

needsLevel.note: The level that building must have reached and finished. values.js needs.tier.

afterYears.note: Game years after which the row opens. values.js afterYears; index.html multiplies by its game-year milliseconds.

power.note: A POWER IS A ROW (decision 8: Adding a power is data, not code), and this is the row - the five fields of The power template, plus its identity. A new ability is a row here and nothing is redeployed; only the fight and the dice that decide a fight ever need replacing (What has to be replaceable when an ability is added). NOTHING READS A POWER YET: neither copy of the fight has an input for one, and M14 item 2 builds that - every place that applies a behaviour must read its amount from this row and never from a fixed list. HELD BACK, both the deployer's: (d) whether a building may carry one - buildingType.abilityId stays as it is until that is answered - and (e) whether a game records the fight's address beside its rules id. And one question the template does not answer, asked in Still open for the deployer: ON WHOM a power acts - its carrier, its neighbours, or everyone on its side. No field for it until it is answered.

id.note: The identity. A number, like buildingType.kindId, so a new power is a new row and no contract is redeployed. item.abilityId points here.

carrierTypeId.note: WHAT CARRIES IT - the weapon, accessory, hat or other item the power lives on, as item.typeId. DECIDED: a power is attached to something, never a loose ability a Friend simply has. Whether that something may also be a building is (d), the deployer's.

amounts.note: WHICH BEHAVIOURS IT TOUCHES, AND BY HOW MUCH - one entry per member of the `behaviour` enum, in its order, zero where the power touches none. A power may touch more than one: Hover is Reach and Speed, Portal is Reach and Sight. The unit of each amount is the economist's.

holders.note: WHO MAY HOLD IT - 'which players are allowed it', the deployer's add-a-power row. Empty for everyone. THE SHAPE IS NOT DECIDED - a list, a role in RareRoles, or a collection; the template says only that the field exists.

usesPerDay.note: USES PER DAY. DECIDED: one a day for every power there is; a power added later states its own on the add-a-power form. A starting value on the deployer page, so a row's field and not a constant.

worth.note: WHAT IT IS WORTH - one number per power, not one per weapon. No value here; the economist's. item.power, the undecided number, was retired into this row.

fightHash.note: THE CHAIN'S HALF OF A FIGHT, and the reason `fight` can live on the server: a hash of the fight's inputs and its result, published AT THE TIME THE FIGHT HAPPENS by the server's RECORD_FIGHT key (A hash of every fight, published as it happens; RareFightLog.commitFight; ruling 18). Write-once per (game, fightId): rewriting it is the one thing the contract exists to make impossible. It does not make the server trustworthy; it makes it auditable - anyone can hash the moves they are shown and compare with what was published on the day. The two fields that are not in the struct are the mapping's keys, marked `key`.

game.note: The mapping's first key. On the contract from its first line because it cannot be added after M20 deploys: a fight id repeats across games.

hash.note: keccak over the fight's inputs and result - combat.js fightHash, BINDING §55. Zero means nothing was committed, so zero may not be written.

blockNumber.note: When it was committed, so 'published before the sync' is checkable rather than trusted.

syncHead.note: HOW THE SERVER'S RECORD AND THE CHAIN'S STAY IN STEP - M3 item 7's open half, as the rulings give it: one head per game-clock HOUR (rulings 16 and 18), BINDING §17's chained word over every move in the period, written once per (game, period) by the RECORD_SYNC key (RareFightLog.commitSync). The sync job backs up the moves and then checks the two records against this; on a mismatch that game's fight writes pause, the deployer is alerted, and the server's record stands until the deployer resolves it (ruling 3). ranking.recomputedScoreboard is the same redundancy from a reader's side. What BINDING.md still owes is the write-up of the fold itself; the shape is here. A bare mapping on the contract, so no struct to hold this to.

period.note: The index of the hourly game-clock period being closed.

head.note: The chained word over the period's moves. Zero means none was written.

base.note: HOME: THE SERVER, since M3 item 5 - the base as it is played is the server's live record, and the chain holds the record of it (see homes.server); four fields below are pinned to the chain because they are property or a commitment, not play. THE BASE'S RECORDED STATE - the first of BINDING §12's eight gaps and the one the other five wait on. It used to be specified only by base.defense() inside index.html, a client belief; since M6 the base has a RECORD in this shape (estate/record.js: ledger, head, moves, apply) and the fight's view is read off it (Record.defense). §10.2, §10.5.2, §10.6 and §10.7 all read it.

id.note: The base. index.html already carries this: BASES, HOME and ofBase(id) exist because every building and every Friend belongs to a base.

ownerTokenId.note: The Genesis token that owns this base. NOT an address: the owner is the token, so selling the base is a token transfer.

crystals.note: What the base holds. Capped by its silo's capacity, which is why the cap is a buildingType field and not a constant. CRYSTALS HAVE NO ON-CHAIN EXISTENCE TODAY - BINDING §20.1 grepped for it and found nothing in any .sol file - and this is the field that gives them one. See `oneHome` and the crystalLedger entity.

wood.note: Level 1 is built of logs. Same standing as crystals: nothing on chain holds it today.

ordersCommit.note: One word per base, the sealed standing orders - BINDING §11.3, and the commitment must predate any fight against it. Declared on the base and not on the fight for exactly that reason: a field on the fight row would be written after the fight exists.

ordersCommitAt.note: When it was sealed. The ordering rule is 'the line-up is committed before the word is requested', and a timestamp is what lets that be checked rather than trusted.

tile.note: A tile a base holds. The claim, not the terrain - the terrain's home is the seed. base.defense() returns baseTiles(id) mapped to x,y pairs and the fight derives its entry vector from the bounding box of exactly this list.

base.note: Who claimed it. index.html's WORLDGEN.claimed maps a tile key to a base id today.

x.note: Tile coordinate, whole numbers. The mockup carries half-tile positions because a building sits in a tile's middle; the CLAIM is whole.

claimedByBuilding.note: The cell that reached it, or zero for the keep's own ground. Ground is claimed by a building's reach, so the record says which - and stepcheck's ladder is a consequence of this field, not a rule beside it.

building.note: One building on one base. Every field BINDING §10.2 says a wall list must come from, and §19.1's row: kind, level, tile, direction for a wall, FINISHED-OR-BUILDING, progress. `!b.build` is load-bearing - an unfinished wall is not a wall - and it is a flag in a page today.

kindId.note: Into buildingType. A number, so a new kind needs no redeploy.

level.note: 1 upward. Every per-level array in buildingType is indexed by this.

x.note: Tile coordinate. The footprint spreads from here by buildingType.footprint.

vert.note: A wall only. Which edge of the tile it stands on: false is the back (north) edge and covers spots (2x, 2y) and (2x+1, 2y); true is the west edge and covers (2x, 2y) and (2x, 2y+1). RareCombat.Wall.vert and combat.js read it the same way, so the SPELLING IS CONSENSUS - index.html calls it dir 'x'/'y' and converts, which is a translation the chain must not inherit.

finished.note: BINDING §10.2: '!b.build is load-bearing and an unfinished wall is not a wall'. A fight must not count it and the page's flag is not a record.

startedAt.note: When it went up. Progress is DERIVED from this plus buildingType.buildMs, not stored - a stored percentage is a second home for a clock.

strengthLeft.note: Damage taken, as what is left. A wall that survived a fight is not a fresh wall, and the record has to say so or the next fight replays against a wall that was already broken.

harvesters.note: A collection depot only, one a depot level (record.js harvester). index.html carries it on the building row already.

hands.note: M8 item 3. The log of how many Friends work this building's build, as pairs [[at, n], ...] in time order (on chain, flattened at, n, at, n), written by the `hands` move; before its first entry one Friend works. Progress is DERIVED from startedAt, buildingType.buildMs, buildingType.hands and this log (record.js worked), never stored. Left off the row when empty.

towerWatch.note: Who is standing watch in a watchtower. §19.1: 'the watchtower's occupant'. One Friend to a tower, and their generation sets the defence while the level sets the reach - so this row is read by the fight and by nothing else.

roster.note: The posted Friend. A ref and not a tokenId, so a Friend cannot be up a tower in a game it never joined.

wallCrew.note: A wall's crew, and EACH MEMBER'S SLOT. BINDING §10.6 is explicit that the slot is part of the truth, not a display detail: the crew stand side by side along the wall's own axis and the slot decides which spot each one occupies, so a fight fought with the slots shuffled is a different fight.

slot.note: Which place along the wall, from zero. Capped by buildingType.capacity. THE SLOT IS THE TRUTH - see the entity note.

rosterRow.note: A posted Friend, per game. BINDING §19.1: { collection, tokenId, gen, x, y, tower, post slot }, and §12 says none of it has a home today. Part one §4.4 says every field of it is chain state. SNAPSHOT AT JOIN, DO NOT RE-READ EACH FIGHT (§4) - which is why gen is stored here having been READ at join, and is not a supplied value.

id.note: The row, so a tower and a wall slot can point at it.

collection.note: The Friend's collection. Stored, not assumed - a partnership fields another collection's tokens.

gen.note: READ from generation(tokenId) AT JOIN and frozen here. Never supplied, never re-read mid-game: re-reading it is how a generation changes under a recorded fight.

postedBy.note: Who posted it, and WHOSE OWNERSHIP WAS CHECKED. For a hired Friend this is the open question - BINDING §13 item 7, undecided.

x.note: IN SPOTS, not tiles. Defenders hold their spots: where you leave a Friend is where it fights.

y.note: In spots. Whole numbers, so a contract can hold the whole fight in integers.

tower.note: Up a watchtower. BINDING §10 ranks a forged value here seventh: it takes two spots of reach off the crew.

order.note: The standing order, set beforehand so the player need not be online. SEALED, not read: BINDING §10 ranks it fifth and §11.3 puts the commitment on the base.

fx.note: The fall-back spot, in spots. Read only for a FALL BACK order.

fy.note: In spots. Read only for a FALL BACK order, and sealed with the order it belongs to.

job.note: Undecided members - see the enum. M3 item 2 requires it.

carrying.note: What it carries - M3 item 2's 'what it carries'. A harvester's haul on its way back to the silo. NO UNIT AND NO CAP DECIDED.

item.note: An item and its power. M3 item 2's shortest noun and the one DESIGN says least about - M14 builds powers and items. Declared so it has a home and so nothing invents one later; every number in it is undecided.

id.note: The item itself, as distinct from its type: two swords of one type are two items.

typeId.note: A registry id, for the same reason buildingType.kindId is: a new item must not be a redeploy.

holder.note: Who has it. An address and not a Friend, until DESIGN says an item is carried rather than owned.

abilityId.note: THE POWER THIS ITEM CARRIES - (c) of What has to be replaceable when an ability is added: a reference to the power row, which is where the amounts and the worth live. The undecided number `item.power` that used to sit beside this was retired into power.amounts and power.worth. The name keeps `ability` because DESIGN's naming row (power / ability) is live and not decided; the row it points at is called power.

uses.note: Whether an item is consumed is not decided.

crystalLedger.note: WHERE A CRYSTAL LIVES - and this entity is a QUESTION WITH A SHAPE, not an answer. BINDING §20.1 checked rather than assumed: grep for crystal and for ore over all five .sol files returns nothing. Crystals live in index.html's purse and are a client belief. A duel is staked in them, so a contract must be able to move them.

shape.note: TWO SHAPES, AND ONE DECIDED RULE ALREADY POINTS AT THE SECOND. (a) an ERC-20 the game mints and burns, or (b) a balance in the game's own storage with an internal transfer. DESIGN's capability table says a player CANNOT 'give crystals or wood to another player, except by staking them in a game' - AN ERC-20 IS FREELY TRANSFERABLE BY DEFINITION, so shape (a) contradicts a decided rule on the day it deploys. That is a collision, not a choice made here. A SECOND CHAIN-ENGINEER IS SPECIFYING THIS IN BINDING AND THIS FILE DEFERS TO IT.

holder.note: Crystals are per base and per game, not per address - which is itself an argument for shape (b), because an ERC-20 balance is per address.

balance.note: Declared here AND on base.crystals. THAT IS A DELIBERATE COLLISION RECORDED IN `oneHome`: exactly one of the two survives, and which one survives is decided by `shape`. It is written down twice here so it cannot be forgotten once.

escrow.note: Staked in a duel and not yet won or returned. With shape (b) there is no safeTransferFrom to call, so the duel and the ledger are either the same contract or the ledger exposes a move-on-behalf function WITH AN ON-CHAIN GUARD - every setter needs one.

overflow.note: THE DEPOT FILLS UP. DESIGN decided the collection depot holds crystals and it fills up; a duel pot can exceed the winner's remaining room, and WHERE AN OVERFLOWING PRIZE GOES IS NOT DECIDED - BINDING §21 item 12. A field with no policy is better than a policy invented here.

fight.note: A fight, and the lifecycle BINDING §12 says has no contract to put it in: a fight id, LinedUp/Rolling/Settled, and the sealing. The row is its INPUTS AND ITS RESULT TOGETHER, never the result alone (§17.2.4) - that is what makes 'fights resolve off chain and the chain records the result' safe rather than a promise, because the recorded result carries everything needed to reproduce it.

id.note: The fight. It is also the roll's batch id, so the same word gives the same fight.

rulesId.note: THE FIELD BINDING §12 SAYS IS MISSING FROM DESIGN'S REPLAY LIST. 'The word, line-ups and spots' does not name the numbers, and a replay of word plus line-up plus spots against a table nobody recorded is not verifiable. Reverts UnknownRules(bytes32) when a fight names a table its game was not created with.

attacker.note: Who came. An address rather than a base, because DESIGN decided anyone may attack.

side.note: One of four. THE ONLY LEGITIMATE INPUT on BINDING §10's list - and even then the vector is derived from the defender's recorded tiles, so there is nothing to validate because nobody supplied it.

gap.note: How far out the line starts, in spots. NO VALUE, AND WHETHER THE ATTACKER PICKS IT IS THE DEPLOYER'S - BINDING §13 item 4. A real tactical lever with three mockup buttons and no ruling. It appears on `rules` too, and `oneHome` records that exactly one of the two is right.

attackers.note: The line-up, by fight slot (0 to 10: a Friend's generation 1 to 6, a 1/1 Doopie 0, an ordinary Doopie's Evolution 1 to 4 as 7 to 10), at most MAX_SIDE. Snapshotted, and each generation READ at line-up rather than supplied. A Doopie never attacks a Doopie (ruling 87).

attackerPower.note: M13 item 19, ruling 116: a Strength power per attacking Friend, in bps of its strength - empty, or one entry per Friend; at most ONE non-zero a side and none above +10% (POWER_CAP_BPS 1000, a constant in combat.js and RareCombat.sol), refused otherwise by both engines. Worked out on the strength it enters with; it ends with the fight and never heals. RareCombat.Setup.attackerPower. The defence's list is RareCombat.Setup.defenderPower, read off the defender's own record (defenderSnapshot). WHICH power a Friend may use, and what it costs, are not this field's: powers are not wired into the game yet.

attackerTokens.note: The tokens behind those generations. gencheck.js's third part is vacuous today because no contract accepts a combat tokenId; THIS FIELD IS WHAT MAKES IT NON-VACUOUS, because a generation must be looked up from a token and not handed over.

defenderSnapshot.note: The hash of the defender's roster rows, walls and tiles as they stood when the fight was lined up. Read from our own storage, never supplied - BINDING §10 items 2, 4, 6 and 7 are all forgeries this one field prevents.

seq.note: The Entropy sequence number. RareDuel's lesson, already paid for: any other sequence's word must be discarded, and an abandoned request's word must not settle anything.

word.note: The Entropy word. One word decides a whole fight; every shot takes the next roll off it.

state.note: LinedUp, Rolling, Settled. `settled` is terminal and one-shot, which is what stops the scoreboard being credited twice - BINDING §16.2, and RareDuel._duel is the working precedent.

ordersOpened.note: The revealed orders, checked against base.ordersCommit. WHO OPENS THEM IS DECIDED - ruling 59: at the fight, by our server as it settles it (RareOrders.reveal behind RECORD_FIGHT, BINDING §78; estate/clockwork.mjs opens them, then commits the fight's hash). WHAT A FIGHT THAT IS NEVER OPENED DOES IS STILL UNDECIDED - BINDING §11.7.

settleDeadline.note: NO VALUE. BINDING §16.4 is blunt that a settlement that never arrives is the live failure, and the two precedents in RareDuel draw the line: where somebody failed to do their part the default punishes them (forfeit); where everybody did their part and the machinery failed the default awards nothing and hands the money back (refundStuck). WHAT A FIGHT'S DEFAULT OUTCOME IS is the deployer's.

There is no second call to forget, no keeper to fall behind and no indexer to crash. game.note: Indexed so a player can fetch a game's whole history with one free log query - step 1 of BINDING §17.3's six free reads.

kind.note: On chain a uint8, the member's index in moveKind, and NOT bounded there: a new kind must not need a new games contract. Undecided members, and the enum's note says why that matters more than it looks: a move kind left off the list is a thing that happened and is not in the record.

parentRoot.note: EVERY BATCH NAMES ITS PARENT. A session's write carries the moveRoot it was built against and is refused if that is not the current root - reverts StaleParent(bytes32 saw, bytes32 is_). AS BUILT, each event's parentRoot is the word THAT MOVE was folded onto, so each event checks against the one before it and the batch's named parent is its first move's. This is the compare-and-swap that closes BOTH the two-clients-out-of-step case the deployer flagged (§16.5) and the replayed-batch half of double-crediting (§16.2), with one comparison and one cold SLOAD.

scoreboard.note: PER PLAYER PER GAME, MAINTAINED MOVE BY MOVE IN THE SAME TRANSACTION AS THE MOVE. Not derived privately off chain and pushed back - that is the natural cheap design and it reintroduces the missed-second-write failure permanently. The RANKING is not here: it is derived, because storing it means writing N players' ranks every time one player moves. HOW THE SCOREBOARD AND THE MOVES STAY IN STEP (M3 item 7's open half, as the rulings give it): the server's session write folds the moves into game.moveRoot and credits this row in the same transaction (move); every fight's hash is public before any sync (fightHash); each hour's head is written once (syncHead) and the sync job checks the two records against it; on a mismatch ruling 3 applies - the server's record stands, the game's fight writes pause, the deployer is alerted. The fold's write-up in BINDING.md is still a chain engineer's; the shape is here.

player.note: Whose row this is. Keyed by address and by game, so one player has one row per game and no global total.

tilesHeld.note: Ground. A count and not a list; the list is `tile`.

fightsLost.note: Attacks that did not, and defences that fell.

stakeIn.note: What this player staked, over every duel in the game. Folded in move by move, so it is the moves and not a separate tally.

The sort order over the stored accumulators - anyone can redo it, nobody has to trust it, and the ranking is not the record: the totals are, and the moves are underneath them. listing.note: A marketplace listing. A base sale is a TOKEN TRANSFER because the Genesis token owns the base, which is the whole payoff of M3 item 8.

collection.note: What kind of thing. A Friend, a Genesis, or zero for an item that is not a token.

itemId.note: For an item rather than a token.

price.note: In $RF - money moves in $RF. No value.

Decision 5: the marketplace's fee does not get the cut's freeze, the deployer's words were 'no need', and the reasoning is sound - a fee on a sale nobody has agreed to yet. The consequence is recorded on scoreboard.stakeOut: any standing figure netted of a sale is not replayable. No value here.

state.note: open, sold, cancelled - not decided as a list. M15's.

shadow.note: A SHADOW: a Solana NFT's stand-in on 4663 - a Doopie, not a Genesis and not a Generation (ruling 35) - written FROM ShadowFriends.sol AS IT IS, for M20 item 1's re-judgement, so that the contract is described here and not the other way round. One row a live shadow, in `shadows[tokenId]`. The token id IS the Solana mint (its raw 32-byte key as a uint256), so a mint has at most one live shadow and the identity needs no second mapping. Soulbound: minted to the claim's `to` and never passed on (`_update` reverts Soulbound on any transfer that is not a mint or a burn). It is created only by `claim` with the attestor's EIP-712 signature (shadowClaim), touched afterwards only by the attestor's `recheck` (checkedAt) and destroyed only by the attestor's `revoke`, which deletes this row, burns the token and frees the mint (shadowFriends.shadowed, shadowFriends.revokedAt). PERMANENT: no proxy and no initializer, so a field that is not here when M21 item 1 deploys can never be added. The fields not in `struct Shadow` are the mapping's key and the ERC-721 owner; each names the line of the contract that holds it (`beside`), and schemacheck greps for it.

tokenId.note: The mapping's key, and the ERC-721 id: uint256(solMint). One identity - anyone can read which shadow belongs to which original by base58-encoding the id.

owner.note: ERC-721 ownerOf: the 4663 wallet the claim named in `to`, which must also be the caller of `claim` (NotYours). Never changes while the shadow lives - a shadow cannot be sold or sent - so it is the address a join guard's ownerOf check passes against, and it is who holds a 1/1 terminal's cut (ruling 54, BINDING §65). It is NOT the Solana holder: that is solOwner, and the two are linked only by the attestor's signature.

mask.note: uint256[16] in the struct - a fixed sixteen words, the type list has no fixed arrays. Which pixels of the 64 x 64 sprite exist: pixel (x, y) is bit y*64+x, most significant first.

palette.note: RGB, three bytes a colour, eight colours to a word. Bounded by the format (at most thirty-two colours), so `revoke` can always clear it.

pixels.note: Five bits a pixel, in reading order over the pixels the mask covers. Bounded like the palette.

colors.note: How many palette entries are real. Refused BadArt above the format's limit.

count.note: How many pixels the mask covers. Refused BadArt above 64 x 64.

solMint.note: THE RAW MINT KEY: the Solana mint's 32-byte public key (b58decode of the address), NEVER A HASH - so the hourly recheck can read it back and ask Solana who holds it. Equal to bytes32(tokenId).

solOwner.note: The Solana wallet that held the mint when it was claimed, as its raw 32-byte key. What the recheck compares Solana's current holder against; a different holder is a revoke.

collection.note: The Solana collection (its update authority), raw 32 bytes. NOT the same thing as rosterRow.collection, which is a 4663 address: a fielded shadow's rosterRow.collection is ShadowFriends' own address and its tokenId is this row's tokenId.

imageHash.note: keccak of the ORIGINAL art, so what was converted can be proved against the source image.

checkedAt.note: THE RECHECK STATE: when the attestor last confirmed the mint is still in solOwner's wallet (recheck, hourly - ruling 16). Set to claimedAt at the claim. NOTHING ON CHAIN READS IT: no contract refuses a shadow whose check has lapsed, so an attestor that stops running leaves every shadow playable. Whether a lapsed check should bar a shadow is not decided anywhere and is not decided here.

name.note: The NFT's name, as the attestor signed it. Unbounded in length; it is cleared by `revoke` with the rest of the row.

traitKeys.note: THE TRAITS, keys as signed: right-padded bytes32, compared byte for byte, at most MAX_TRAITS, no zero key and no key twice (claim refuses BadTraitKey, DuplicateTrait, TooManyTraits), so traitOf has exactly one answer. RareDoopieGate.isOneOfOne reads `Evolution` here - the one on-chain consumer of a trait.

traitValues.note: The values, the same length as traitKeys (TraitsMismatch otherwise). As ATTESTED, not as the collection reads today: they vouch for the signature, not for Solana (BINDING B1.8).

shadowClaim.note: WHAT THE ATTESTOR SIGNS, and the only way a shadow comes into being: the calldata of ShadowFriends.claim, an EIP-712 message in the domain 'Rare Fiends Shadows' version '1'. Never stored - its art, keys and traits are copied into a `shadow` row and `to` becomes the owner - but its SHAPE is the most permanent thing in the bridge: CLAIM_TYPEHASH and the domain are frozen into every signature the attestor will ever make, so a field added, removed or reordered is a new contract and a new attestor. schemacheck holds the struct, the typehash string and this row to one order. The attestor that signs it is shadowFriends.attestor.

to.note: The 4663 wallet that may redeem it - and must be the caller (NotYours). The whitelist is asked about the caller before anything else (roles.requireAllowed, ruling 21).

solMint.note: The raw mint key; becomes the token id. Refused AlreadyShadowed while a live shadow holds it, and ClaimPredatesRevoke if it was signed at or before the mint's last revoke.

solOwner.note: The Solana holder the attestor read, raw 32 bytes.

mask.note: uint256[16]: the sprite's mask, as shadow.mask.

palette.note: As shadow.palette; refused BadArt past the format's word count.

pixels.note: As shadow.pixels; refused BadArt past the format's word count.

deadline.note: When the signature stops being redeemable (ClaimExpired). The attestor signs now + CLAIM_TTL, so deadline - CLAIM_TTL is when it was signed - which is the only clock a claim carries, and what lets claim refuse one signed before a revoke.

traitKeys.note: As shadow.traitKeys, checked here rather than trusted.

shadowFriends.note: THE SHADOW CONTRACT'S OWN STATE - what is per contract or per Solana mint rather than per live shadow, the way `roles` is RareRoles'. Every field here names the line that holds it (`beside`) and schemacheck greps ShadowFriends.sol for it. The guards, all on chain: claim is the attestor's signature plus the whitelist plus `to == msg.sender`; recheck and revoke are `msg.sender == attestor`; setAttestor is the SET_ATTESTOR power in RareRoles (ruling 60).

attestor.note: THE ATTESTOR: the key that signs claims and alone may recheck and revoke. A plain stored address, changeable - never zero (WrongSigner). The attestor service holds the key; who may REPLACE it is the roles system's (setAttestorPower, ruling 60).

setAttestorPower.note: SET_ATTESTOR, the one power that may change the attestor, held in RareRoles (ruling 60): root holds it by being root, the gamemaster once granted it (grant.mjs), and a leaked holder is removed in RareRoles without touching this contract. It was `immutable team`, which would have made a lost key permanent. Each change logs AttestorChanged.

roles.note: RareRoles, immutable: the launch whitelist claim asks FIRST (ruling 21), and the holder of SET_ATTESTOR. recheck and revoke do not ask the whitelist, so closing the gate never strands a revoke.

claimTtl.note: How long a signed claim lives. A constant because revoke needs it (a claim signed before a revoke must not land after it), held equal to attestor.mjs CLAIM_TTL by the parity check. Its value is in the contract, not here.

maxTraits.note: The most traits a shadow carries - public so a reader knows the scan traitOf is bounded by.

shadowed.note: One LIVE shadow per mint, keyed by the raw mint key. Set by claim, cleared by revoke - so a mint is NOT once ever: a Doopie sold on Solana is bridged again by its buyer (BINDING B3).

revokedAt.note: THE REVOKE STATE, per mint, and it OUTLIVES the shadow it revoked: when the mint's shadow was last revoked, zero if never. claim refuses any claim whose deadline <= revokedAt + CLAIM_TTL (ClaimPredatesRevoke), so the seller's still-valid calldata cannot re-shadow a sold Doopie (found by bridge-proof.mjs, 2026-09-30).

switch.note: M19 ITEM 8, THE SWITCH MECHANISM ITSELF - BUILT in RareRoles (BINDING §64.4, 2026-10-01; not deployed). A switch is a NAME AND A BIT, held by the one mechanism and read by the contract that obeys it (requireSwitchOn(key), reverting SwitchOff(key)), never a flag inside that contract - so one mechanism serves the four things DESIGN rides on it: a tradeable asset's switch, a whole collection on or off, more than one partnership (one at a time at launch - built, not live), and the technology centre (built and switched off). Its home is RareRoles (BINDING §64.4), beside the powers it is guarded by. Every switch is OFF until turned on: an unwritten key reads false, which is DESIGN's 'closed until we open it'. Setting one logs switchSet and refuses a no-op (SwitchUnchanged), like DemoModeUnchanged; it needs no delay (M19 item 9: confirmed on the page, instant on chain). ONE INSTANCE PREDATES THE MECHANISM AND STAYS: RareMarket.tradeable[collection] behind SET_TRADEABLE. RareMarket is permanent, so that switch is not moved into this one; it is the same switch in shape - a name and a bit, its own power, a log, a refused no-op - and the deployer page is to list both side by side. BUILT: RareRoles.switchOn, requireSwitchOn and setSwitch, proved by contracts/test/fixcheck.js part 28. No contract obeys a switch yet.

key.note: The mapping's key: keccak256("rarefriends.switch." + name). THE SAME WORD IS THE POWER THAT FLIPS IT, so there is no second table pairing switches with powers. A per-collection switch names the collection in its name ("collection." + its lowercase hex address); a per-kind tradeable switch, a partnership slot and the technology centre each have a plain name.

name.note: OVERRIDDEN HOME. The readable name the deployer page lists and hashes into `key`. The chain holds only the hash, so the list of names is the page's, and the page proves each by recomputing the key and reading it back.

on.note: The bit. False until it is turned on.

power.note: DERIVED: equal to `key`. A narrow power in RareRoles (M19 item 10): root holds every one, and root grants a gamemaster exactly the switches it may flip with grantPower(key, GAMEMASTER, true) - the partnership switch without the trade switches. A switch root wants kept to itself is registerRootPower(key), irreversibly. So the setter is guarded on chain by hasPower(msg.sender, key).

beside: function setSwitch(bytes32 key, bool on) external {
heldWhileGameRuns.note: DECIDED, ruling 74 (DESIGN, 2026-10-01): 'No switch changes once a game has started' - TRUE FOR EVERY SWITCH, not per switch. setSwitch asks requireNoGameRunning() after the power and before the no-op check, so a stranger gets PowerNotHeld and never learns a game runs. The tradeable switch is frozen the same way (RareMarket.setTradeable, BINDING §80); the market FEE is a number with its own exemption, not a switch. Reading (requireSwitchOn) is never frozen.

switchSet.note: THE RECORD OF EVERY SWITCH CHANGE - M19 item 9's 'every change is recorded' for the switch, and the only history of it: the mapping holds the present, this event holds how it got there. One event per accepted change; a refused no-op logs nothing. BUILT with `switch`: RareRoles.SwitchSet.

key.beside: event SwitchSet(bytes32 indexed key, bool on, address indexed by);
key.note: Which switch. Indexed so the deployer page fetches one switch's history in one log query.

by.note: Who flipped it - the deployer or a gamemaster holding the power. The same shape as DemoModeSet(on, by).

note: THE ONE HOME'S INDEX. values.js carries every chain-homed number; this says which schema field each
one is, so a value with no field in the schema cannot be added quietly (schemacheck resolves every
entry here against `entities`) and the schema cannot describe a value that nothing holds. A key that
maps to an entity rather than a field is a table whose shape the entity gives (kinds, weapons,
combat, startBase). `kindRow` does the same for the columns of a kind's row; `sub` is display copy and
says so. `readers` are the places that must READ the file - the proof that M3 items 1 and 3 are code
and not a drawing: if any of these strings leaves its file, the check goes red.
